hero.title: Who we answer to.
hero.subtitle: The public record of our stakeholder governance under B Corp PSG 2.1 — the six groups we have identified and prioritized, how their interests enter our decisions, and the engagement mechanisms that keep every one of them represented.

map.title: Six stakeholder groups, mapped and prioritized.
map.lead: We identify stakeholders by three tests: how directly company decisions touch them, how dependent they are on the platform, and how much influence they hold over it. Workers, suppliers and customers come out primary — they are daily operating partners. Investors, community and environment are strategic — engaged through structured cycles rather than daily operations, with the environment represented through monitoring and verification rather than dialogue.

groups.name: Workers
groups.who: The founder-led team that builds and runs the platform — engineering, operations and hub presence across three regions.
interests: A voice in what gets built

groups.name: Suppliers
groups.who: The 150+ artisans and ateliers across handloom clusters who make everything the platform sells.

groups.name: Customers
groups.who: The buyers and brands who purchase handcrafted goods on the platform's storefronts.
interests: A fair price for what craft costs

groups.name: Investors
groups.who: Pre-seed and seed backers of the company's current raise.

groups.name: Community
groups.who: The craft clusters and cities that host our hubs, offices and ateliers — Bagru, Srinagar, Florence, Sydney.

groups.name: Environment
groups.who: The commons that absorbs production's footprint — engaged through monitoring, verification and review rather than dialogue.

decisions.title: Stakeholder interests don't just get heard — they get decided with.
decisions.lead: Engagement is not a survey we file away. Interests raised through the mechanisms below change what we build, how we price, and what the board holds itself to.

cards.body: The partner portal is mobile-first with no portals to learn because that is what artisans could actually use. What gets built next starts with what artisans, buyers and the team can operate — not with what is elegant in a spec.

Commission and payout terms are published and queryable. When artisans raise issues with settlements, that feedback goes directly into how terms policy is written — transparency is the default, not a concession.
The board-adopted purpose statement binds strategy to stakeholder outcomes, and its annual review covers what each group actually experienced — not what we intended.
Custom-order consults — measurements, fabric, fit — flow straight into techpacks and sizing standards. Buyer interests literally shape the product specification.

mechanisms.title: Every group, represented by mechanisms that exist today.
mechanisms.lead: The full inventory of engagement mechanisms, per stakeholder group. Each one is live now — not planned, not aspirational.

groups.name: Workers of the company
items: Weekly all-hands — direction, open decisions and results reviewed with the whole team
Direct founder access — every teammate has an open line to the CEO
Written feedback channels — concerns and suggestions logged and actioned

groups.name: Suppliers
items: Mobile production portal — runs, accept/decline and live progress chat on their phone
WhatsApp rails — updates and conversation on channels artisans already use
In-person hub visits — onboarding and atelierside visits in Bagru, Srinagar and Florence
Payout transparency — published commission, reviewable terms and settlement queries
Structured feedback — periodic surveys and interviews on tools, terms and rails

groups.name: Customers
items: Contact & demo flow — contact page, waitlist and demo conversations
Storefront reviews — reviews and testimonials collected at the storefronts
Social channels — Instagram and Facebook catalogs, DMs as feedback loops
Custom-order consults — measurements, fabric and fit feed directly into specs

groups.name: Investors
items: Digital investor room — the pre-seed round runs through the shared app at investors.jaalyantra.com
Public investor page — thesis, traction and raise in the open
Direct founder line — every investor talks to the CEO, not a proxy

groups.name: Community
items: On-the-ground presence — the team works from the hubs; atelier relationships are the community link
Local partnerships — Indian Handloom Council, Startup India, Startup Latvia
Community events — meetups, exhibitions and market visits in the clusters

groups.name: The environment
items: Per-run materials ledger — dye, weave and finish logged with quantities and timestamps
Verification gates — certifications such as GOTS checked on-platform before a lot can ship; a Digital Product Passport on every piece
Low-waste logistics — shipments consolidated through hubs; made-to-order means no deadstock
Water & dye practices — natural indigo vats and fibre washing governed by certification checks
Electricity consumption — monitored across the company's hubs and facilities

criteriaMap.requirement: The company identifies and prioritizes its stakeholders and maps the stakeholders listed in 2.1.3
